title: The Window of Tolerance
subtitle: Finding your optimal zone for healing and growth

sections.heading: What is the Window of Tolerance?
sections.content:
Developed by Dr. Dan Siegel, the Window of Tolerance describes the zone where you can experience and integrate emotions without becoming overwhelmed or shutting down.

Within your window:
• You can think clearly
• You can feel emotions without being flooded
• You can connect with others
• You can handle normal life stressors

This is your ventral vagal zone - where healing and growth happen.

sections.heading: Above the Window: Hyperarousal
sections.content:
When pushed above your window, you enter hyperarousal (sympathetic activation):

• Anxiety or panic
• Racing thoughts
• Feeling overwhelmed
• Irritability or rage
• Difficulty sleeping
• Hypervigilance

You're in fight/flight mode - too much energy, too little grounding.
sections.practicePrompt: What pushes you into hyperarousal? What are your early warning signs that you're leaving your window upward?

sections.heading: Below the Window: Hypoarousal
sections.content:
When pushed below your window, you enter hypoarousal (dorsal vagal shutdown):

• Numbness or emptiness
• Disconnection from body
• Depression or flatness
• Exhaustion or collapse
• Brain fog
• Feeling frozen

You're in freeze mode - too little energy, too much shutdown.
sections.practicePrompt: What pushes you into hypoarousal? How do you know when you're shutting down?

sections.heading: Your Window Can Change
sections.content:
Your window of tolerance isn't fixed. It can:

• Narrow when you're stressed, tired, or triggered
• Expand with safety, rest, and support
• Shrink after trauma or prolonged stress
• Grow through healing work and practice

On hard days, be gentle with yourself - your window may be smaller than usual.
sections.practicePrompt: Notice how your window changes throughout the day. What makes it smaller? What helps it expand?

sections.heading: Expanding Your Window
sections.content:
You can gradually widen your window of tolerance through:

• Titration: Approaching difficult things in small doses
• Pendulation: Moving between activation and calm
• Resourcing: Building up positive experiences
• Co-regulation: Being with safe people
• Grounding: Staying connected to your body

The goal isn't to never leave your window, but to recognize when you have and know how to return.
sections.practicePrompt: What resources help you return to your window? Make a list of things that help you feel grounded and safe.

sections.heading: Working at the Edges
sections.content:
Growth happens at the edges of your window - gently stretching into discomfort while staying regulated. This is different from being pushed out.

Safe stretching looks like:
• Feeling challenged but not overwhelmed
• Staying connected to your body
• Having support available
• Being able to pause when needed

With practice, what once pushed you out of your window becomes manageable within it.
sections.practicePrompt: What's one small edge you could work with this week? Something slightly challenging but not overwhelming?
